prompts.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes or contributed to group efforts over time.

Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced.
Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom.
What have you done to make your school or your community a better place?
Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?

intl_finance.document: Financial documents (bank statements for personal or sponsor funds, or award/sponsor letters) showing funds that meet or exceed ISEO's one-academic-year estimate (3 quarters / 9 months for undergraduates), submitted with the new-admit I-20 request in iServices
intl_finance.notes: ISEO treats newly admitted students as those who have accepted an offer of admission. All documents must be dated within 3 months of submission, be in English or have an official certified translation, and show funds that are immediately available (not frozen or locked). Bank statements should be a concise 1-2 pages without transaction history; dependents need extra funding. The dollar estimates are in tables that did not load in text, so no amount is recorded. No date is published.

notes: The 8 Personal Insight Questions are the same for all UC campuses (answer 4, max 350 words each); text copied from the UC Admissions page (source 1), which does not print a cycle year. Source 2 (UC counselor guide titled 2026-27) confirms the same format for the 2026-27 application: respond to 4 of the 8 questions, 350 words maximum per response. The UC application also has optional Additional comments boxes (source 2); they are not essay prompts and are not listed here. UC San Diego's own page (source 4) repeats that you must answer 4 of 8 questions with a 350-word limit per answer, and lists a Portfolio Review that is optional for Arts majors (its contents were not captured); no other written questions were found.
